new_statements.quote: p.174: „Das Ur-Ambon betonte alle mehr als einsilbigen Wörter auf der Pänultima des Grundwortes.“ — p.175: „In anderen SA.-Sprachen führte das starre Festhalten an dieser Betonungsweise zum Verstummen des Stützvokales. Hierher gehören die Sprachen von Piru, Kamarian u. a.“ — p.76 (§ 79 b): „Kamarian, Tihulale, Kaibobo, Piru. UA. Hamza blieb erhalten; der Stützvokal ist wieder verloren gegangen (vgl. § 145)“ — p.110 (§ 125): „Der gleiche Schwund des Vokals, der zwischen den beiden ursprünglich betonten Silben stand, findet sich auch gelegentlich im Kaibobo, Kamarian, Paulohi, Amahei und Nuetetu (SA.), z. B.: gestern Kb. henmása […] Zinn Kb. supkái < *súpikái, fragen Kb. atnéu < *á-ta-néu.“
new_statements.translation: p.174: 'Ur-Ambon stressed all words of more than one syllable on the penult of the base word.' — p.175: 'In other Sub-Ambon languages the rigid retention of this way of stressing led to the silencing of the support vowel. To this group belong the languages of Piru, Kamarian and others.' — p.76 (§ 79 b): 'Kamarian, Tihulale, Kaibobo, Piru. Ur-Ambon glottal stop was retained; the support vowel has been lost again (cf. § 145)' — p.110 (§ 125): 'The same loss of the vowel that stood between the two originally stressed syllables is also found occasionally in Kaibobo, Kamarian, Paulohi, Amahei and Nuetetu (Sub-Ambon), e.g.: yesterday Kb. henmása […] tin Kb. supkái < *súpikái, ask Kb. atnéu < *á-ta-néu.'

new_statements.relation_note: The catalog has no record and no existing statement for kaib1244, so this is the first placement evidence: penult of the base, by inference from the SA. rule plus the p.76 grouping plus three accented Kaibobo forms; no sentence of the form 'das Kaibobo betont..' exists in the text that could be reached. How opened: the listed HathiTrust copy (hdl.handle.net/2027/coo.31924009725965) is could not be reached by automated download (2 tries, plus the imgsrv plaintext endpoint 'Blocked from HathiTrust'); the Google Books full view (BcFfVmh_otoC) refuses page images, click3 JSON and in-volume search (403 on books.google.com.uk.au.in, browser headers included), while the Google Books Atom feed stil…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Stress on the penultimate syllable of the base word (the Ur-Ambon/Sub-Ambon pattern), stated for Kaibobo only indirectly: the general SA. rule (p.174); Kaibobo is listed (p.76) with Piru, Kamarian and Tihulale among the languages that dropped the support vowel again, the change that p.175 attributes to keeping the base-penult stress ('Piru, Kamarian u. a.'); and the only accent-marked Kaibobo words the snippets expose, henmása 'yesterday', supkái 'tin', atnéu 'ask' (p.110), plus pretonic-vowel loss Kb. nana < anana, mrua < *marua (p.108), carry the stress on the penult of the syncopated word. Whether Kaibobo suffixes shift the stress (Paulohi/Sepa type) or leave it on the base (Asilulu/Piru type) is not stated; the grouping with Piru/Kamarian makes the latter more likely, but that is inference.
new_statements.secondary_stress: Nothing for Kaibobo. The book's four-syllable Ur-Ambon words carry two accents (sába-kúku, málu-málu, kásawári); in Kaibobo the vowel between the two old stresses is lost and the second stress remains (henmása, supkái, atnéu).
new_statements.exceptions: None for Kaibobo. The p.110 loss is said to occur only 'gelegentlich' (occasionally). No Kaibobo item appears under § 177 b)-g) (possessive, personal, derivational, nominal, plural and numeral suffixes); the feed returns nothing for 'Kb.'/'Kaibobo' with Pluralzeichen, Zahlwörter, Akzent, betont, Pänultima, Ultima, or Pepet+betont.
new_statements.identity_note: Stresemann's 'Kb.' = the village Kaibobo on the south coast of West Seram (p.13 abbreviations; p.10 'Die Dörfer Eti, Kaibobo, Waisamu und Hatusua folgen einander an der Südküste Westserans'); 'E.' = Eti, 'HS.' = Hatasua, 'WS.' = Waisamu are the sister villages of the same West-Littoral language. He classes them as Sub-Ambon and, for the glottal stop and the support vowel (§ 79 b, p.76), groups Kaibobo with Kamarian, Tihulale and Piru rather than with Eti/Waisamu/Hatusua; the source of his Kaibobo wordlist is not visible in the pages reached (the p.2 source list was read but names no Kaibobo item; van Ekris 1864-65 is the likely printed source).

new_statements.quote: Moreover, it displays a conditioned split of *ə, based on stress differences, although there are some exceptions presumably caused by borrowing from West Piru Bay languages.
new_statements.citation: Collins, James T. 1982. Linguistic Research in Maluku: A Report of Recent Field Work. Oceanic Linguistics 21(1/2): 73-146, esp. pp. 122-123 (Teor-Kur).

new_statements.second_reader_evidence: Held copy (74 pp., ProQuest scan; extracted text yields only the 210-byte cover line, so no text layer). Page image (printed p. 98, PDF p. 26/74, section 3.1.8 'West Littoral Seram') shows exactly: 'Moreover, it displays a conditioned split of *ə, based on stress differences, although there are some exceptions presumably caused by borrowing from West Piru Bay languages.' The scanned file scanned/ / line 1087-1090 has the same sentence with *e for *ə (scanned limitation; image is authoritative). The whole section 3.1.8 (pp. 98-99) gives Kaibobo's *w loss, absence of *p reflex and the *ə split; it says nothing about which syllable carries stress, so none found is right. Identity: p. 98 'Kaibo…
new_statements.relation_note: Language is not in the catalog. Compatible with the existing Stresemann 1927 inference (fixed penult of the base word for the Ambon/Seram group) and with Collins 1983 p.65/fn.88, which give the same stress-conditioned *ə split in more detail; adds only that Kaibobo has word stress that conditions vowel reflexes. Nothing on placement, so it neither confirms nor contradicts penultimate stress. The only other stress mention in the article (pp. 96-97) concerns Luhu (West Piru Bay): fossilized suffixes -ne/-e/-a 'resulted in new stress patterns' with antepenultimate vowel deletion (**kalulan-a > kallana 'wave') - not about Kaibobo. The 'esp. pp. 122-123 (Teor-Kur)' locator in the citation is abo…
new_statements.rule_in_words: No placement rule. The sentence only presupposes that Kaibobo has word stress (a reflex of Proto-Central-Maluku *ə is conditioned by stressed vs unstressed position); it does not say which syllable is stressed. The article is a survey of field work and classification, with no phonology/prosody section for any language.
new_statements.exceptions: Only exceptions to the *ə split (attributed to borrowing from West Piru Bay languages), not exceptions to a stress rule.
new_statements.identity_note: Collins 1982 p. 98 defines Kaibobo as the language of four villages, Eti, Kaibobo, Waesamu and Hatusua (plus resettled speakers at Ariate across Piru Bay, fn. 13), with 'little dialectal variation'; the stress remark is about this language as a whole, not a specific village dialect. The Luhu/Piru stress remark on pp. 96-97 is about a different (West Piru Bay) language.

sources.note: No statement of where Kaibobo stress falls. p.65: 'Kaibobo displays **e > e but **ə > e, when stressed, o when unstressed.[87] In words containing two occurrences of **ə the unstressed **ə > o by assimilation.' fn.88 p.145: 'unstressed **ə in Kaibobo regularly became e'.
